newsitem.title: UK: UK prompt spot natgas eases, other periods steady.
newsitem.headline: UK prompt spot natgas eases, other periods steady.

text.p: The prompt U.K. natural gas market eased slightly lower on Thursday but the rest of the forward curve held steady.
Day ahead gas was actively traded, with deals done at a low of 11.25 pence a therm, 0.25 pence down on Wednesday's trades.
June also slipped lower over the course of the day, trading at 11.30 p/th in the morning before dipping to trade at 11.10 p/th later.
"Everything on the prompt side has come off," said one trader.
The June IPE contract came off the board at the close of business on Thursday. Physical delivery against the expiry will be announced on Friday, an IPE spokeswoman said.
Further out, levels were stable, but reflecting the IPE market, the whole forward curve was better offered than bid.
"It's all within range," a trader said.
The third quarter of this year traded at 11.05 p/th and the fourth quarter fetched 13.75 p/th.
Other traders were looking further ahead with a deal done for the first quarter 1999 at 16.90 p/th.
All reported trade on Thursday was at the National Balancing Point (NBP), with buying interest for St.Fergus gas scant.
